summary: Registers the audio/mpeg media type so that MPEG-1 and MPEG-2 audio files, such as MP3, can be labeled consistently in email and on the web. Before this, there was no uniform MIME type for them. It is on the standards track.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC registers audio/mpeg as the MIME media type for MPEG-1 and MPEG-2 audio. It also records encoding and security guidance for sending the data.

questions: what is the mime type for mp3
what is the mime type for mpeg audio
what file extensions use audio mpeg
what security warning applies to audio mpeg
subtitle: The registered MIME media type for MPEG-1 and MPEG-2 audio streams.

tldr.problem: MPEG audio was used on the Internet without a uniform MIME media type for identifying it.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC registers audio/mpeg for MPEG audio frames from MPEG-1 and MPEG-2, with no parameters.
tldr.outcome: The registration gives systems a shared media type; the RFC also warns that tagged streams could contain executable material.

today: RFC 3003 is a Proposed Standard. The unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: What audio/mpeg Identifies
sections.content:
The MPEG-1 and MPEG-2 standards define audio layers I, II, and III. Compressed audio is split into frames with a frame header and audio data. The audio/mpeg type identifies an elementary byte stream containing MPEG frames, possibly with non-MPEG data interspersed.

The RFC notes that MPEG audio was designed for streaming rather than as a file format and does not define a standard way to include metadata.
sections.plainLanguage: The media type identifies a stream of MPEG audio frames. The audio format itself does not define one standard way to attach metadata.

sections.title: Registration and Encoding
sections.content:
The registered type is audio/mpeg, with no required or optional parameters. For non-binary transport such as email, the binary audio data must be encoded; the RFC says Base64 is suitable for email.

The registration lists the file extensions .mp1, .mp2, and .mp3. It says lower layers are assumed to handle transmission errors, so MPEG frames may omit optional CRCs for improved audio quality.
sections.plainLanguage: The type has no extra parameters. Since the audio is binary, email needs an encoding such as Base64 to carry it.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
MPEG is a tagged data format, and private-use tags could carry arbitrary material, including executable content. Tagged data containing executable content SHOULD never be sent and MUST NOT be executed when received.

Audio/mpeg objects are not internally signed or encrypted. The RFC says external security mechanisms are needed for confidentiality.
sections.plainLanguage: An MPEG stream may contain more than audio, including executable content. Do not execute such content, and use external protections when confidentiality is needed.

references.text: Bradner, S., "Key words for use in RFCs to Indicate Requirement Levels", BCP 14, RFC 2119, March 1997.
